comment: Shared hostname-matching vectors. Checked by proxy/policy_core_test.py, src/policy.test.ts AND the Corefile expression builder (src/services/coredns/config.test.ts) so the TypeScript, Python and DNS matchers can never disagree. A bare name is EXACT; *.name is subdomains only.
path_comment: http-filter path glob: the same * as host names, with / in the role of . (a lone * segment spans any depth; * inside a segment stays within it). Request paths are matched without the query string, percent-decoded once. Checked by proxy/policy_core_test.py; src/inputs.test.ts checks the pattern validation.
git_comment: Paths on a git host (GIT_HOSTS: github.com): case-insensitive, and one .git suffix is dropped from every segment of both the path and the pattern, so every spelling of a repository gets the same verdict (and *.git is a one-segment *). git_pattern_keys: two patterns with the same key are duplicates on a git host.
selftest_comment: The action's own setup probe (src/setup/selftest.ts repointSelfTest; proxy/policy_core.py is_selftest_probe), exempt from http-filter.
redact_comment: Redaction of what the report prints from the job's traffic. Labels: src/report/redact.ts looksEncoded (refused names) and proxy/suggest.py looks_encoded (names in a suggestion) must agree; both run these. boundary_labels sit on each side of every threshold the two copies share (LONG_LABEL_LEN, ENCODED_MIN_LEN, HEX_MIN_LEN, SHORT_HEX_LEN, MAX_VOWEL_RATIO, MIN_DIGIT_RUNS, ENTROPY_MIN_LEN, ENTROPY_BITS), most of them caught by that rule alone, so a change to a constant on one side only fails a test. (HEX_MIN_LEN below ENCODED_MIN_LEN changes nothing: shorter labels return first.) Path segments (proxy/suggest.py path_segment_shown, checked by proxy/suggest_test.py) are stricter: a hidden one becomes * in a suggestion. standard_methods: the only methods a report or suggestion names.

suggest_comment: Suggested http-filter (proxy/suggest.py): allowed requests -> expected suggestion. proxy/suggest_test.py checks the output and the round trip (suggestion -> policy.json -> policy_core allows every request in replay, or in requests, and refuses every request in refuse); src/report.test.ts renders each expected suggestion as YAML, reads it back as the action reads the input, and checks the policy it builds with the same engine.

suggest.name: a read-only host collapses to one line
reads split from writes; write paths templated, ids never echoed
a few literals at one position stay pinned
more than MAX_PINNED literals at one position become *
git push and fetch stay pinned to the repos used (one spelling per repo on github.com)
many pushed-to repos are templated, and the suggestion says it is coarse
method-boundary trap: a broad POST rule never re-opens pushes
the NONE guard sits under the broad rule, so it outranks it
no NONE guard where nothing broad could match a pack path
encoded-looking names and GitHub platform hosts are left out
a segment that could break the YAML or the engine is never pasted
only standard methods go into a rule
path segments that look like data become *
round trip: trailing slash, ;params, //, escapes, git spellings, paths cut short in the log

sudo_comment: sudo-config command lines (src/services/sudo/config.ts parseSudoLine / ruleAllows; proxy/sudo_suggest.py suggests only lines that parse). valid: the parsed rule; invalid: refused. match: what a rule allows, as the sudo log records a command (absolute path, arguments joined by spaces): exact arguments; a trailing * takes ONE OR MORE further arguments (classic sudo needs the space before *, sudo-rs takes zero or more: both allow this). suggest: observed workflow commands -> the suggested rules and omitted counts.

suggest.name: never a wildcard: many installs stay exact lines
secrets, unwritable lines and other users are left out and counted
short password flags and environment variables
